title: log.jsonl — one event (one line)
$comment: One line of log.jsonl: what happened, appended by the tool and never rewritten. The thread's state (lifecycle, claims, counts, links) and index.md are computed from it; its metadata is thread.yml's, edited directly, and hand edits there aren't events. Every event has the same envelope (id, ts, by, type, payload), and the set of types is closed.

then.description: First event of every thread. Folder laid out, origin.md and thread.yml written. The payload is the initial metadata (the baseline for the view's 'thread.yml since the thread began' line until the first checkpoint) plus the namespace it was created in.

supersedes.description: Legacy: supersede was retired; never written now.

then.description: Presence, not ownership: several sessions can claim a thread. Liveness is derived from the session's last event on the thread.

intent.description: Optional. One line shown in the presence banner, so another session knows what this one is doing.

then.description: The session stops working on the thread; its claim goes away.

skipped-checkpoint.description: Reason given to --skip, if the release bypassed a due checkpoint.

session.description: Session released by doctor when it differs from the event author.

then.description: `at` is the latest event the author had read; the append succeeds only if it is still the latest. The body lives in checkpoints/<checkpoint>.md.

headline.description: Duplicated from the file's frontmatter so the arc renders from the log alone. Same cap.

registers.description: Registrations made in this checkpoint. Reserved; the tool records registrations as `register` events.

then.description: A finding. Never shown by `view`; searchable with `replay`. Uncapped.
Written when tasks.yml changes, through a command or through a hand edit the tool diffs on its next command. `task-edited` covers hand edits that change a task's text.

hand-edit.description: True when detected by diff rather than issued by a command.

from.description: Thread this task was rolled up from at merge.

then.description: On the PARENT. A subthread started, directly or by promoting a task. History for the parent's arc and counts; the subthreads list itself comes from scanning the store for threads whose thread.yml names this parent.

On the PARENT, one per merge. The child's log isn't replayed: the parent gets this event plus a forced checkpoint. It carries the child's final checkpoint (the merge report), what was copied, what stayed behind as a pointer, and which tasks rolled up.

checkpoint.description: The child's final checkpoint id — the merge report.

headline.description: The child's final checkpoint headline, copied so the parent's view can show it without opening the child.

pointers.description: Registered child items left in the child and pointed at from the parent's index.

tasks.description: Ids the rolled-up tasks were given on the parent's board.

forced.description: True when --force reparented the child's own open children.

then.description: A doc or artifact registered on the thread, or the reading guide written or changed. index.md is the fold over these.

from.description: For a copy made at merge: the `<thread>@<cid>` it came from.

pointer.description: An item left in another thread: `<thread>:<path>@<cid>`. Nothing is copied; the index shows it as a pointer.

then.description: A thread state transition. The doctor writes active→inactive for threads untouched for a while; the tool writes inactive→active before any other event on an inactive thread.

reason.description: Free text. The doctor gives its reason for shelving; the tool writes reopened. Older logs may also carry merged, closed or superseded, which the fold uses to tell a legacy merge from a legacy close.

successor.description: Legacy supersede pointer; never written now.

superseded-by.description: Legacy supersede pointer; never written now.

then.description: The origin was replaced in place after a clean checkpoint; the prior file remains beside it.
A dated revision section was appended under the origin's '## Revisions'.
Add or remove a one-sided thread relationship.
On the CHILD. Records the merge, so the child's content and log stay as they were.

checkpoint.description: The parent's merge checkpoint, known in advance (next ordinal).

then.description: On the PARENT. Legacy, read but never written: a child closed without merging. History only; the child's own log says how it ended.
On the PARENT. A child was dropped (not worth pursuing). A normal ending: shown on the parent's view page and never a doctor finding.
On the PARENT. A finished child was reopened.
Legacy parent event from the retired supersede command; never written now.
On the NEW PARENT, paired with `reparented` on the moved thread. History, like `child-created`; the subthreads list comes from the child's thread.yml.

from.description: The parent it was moved away from.

then.description: On the MOVED thread, as history: the tool writes the new parent to thread.yml at the same time, and nothing reads the parent from this event (older versions did). No folder moves, since subthreads live flat beside their parents.
On the thread being reopened, immediately before its state-changed from a final state (completed, dropped, merged) to active.
